chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from the one who heard Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying:
Do not expend from yourself for your brethren what is more harmful to you than it is beneficial for them.

key_terms.إِخْوَانِكَ: your brethren (plural of brother, referring to fellow believers)
key_terms.نَفْسِكَ: yourself (referring to one's own self, energy, or essence)

ai.seo_question: How much should one give to others without harming themselves?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) advises believers to exercise prudence in their acts of kindness and generosity towards their brethren. One should not give so much of themselves (time, energy, wealth) that the harm or burden to themselves exceeds the benefit gained by the recipient, ensuring that charity does not become a source of detriment. This principle, rooted in the Shia tradition of *ihsan* balanced with *hikmah*, prevents the giver from becoming a burden to the community or losing their own stability, thereby preserving the sustainability of social bonds.
